episodes.podcast_title: Evan Carmichael - Believe: Unlocking Your True Potential
episodes.description:
✎ Get free access to our vault of PDF summaries for every YouTube video here: https://believe.evancarmichael.com/the-vault ✎ Check out my NEWEST video: https://goo.gl/E0eE6m ✎ To get more details on all the research and studies mentioned in this video check out the articles below: https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg-new-years-resolutions-list-2018-1 https://docs.google.com/document/d/15vzdkeFh1jKEz9QJWGZxUQomN3IetsDehiJHJ7PQ51Q/edit?tab=t.ei5qqx99fn8b https://www.theguardian.com/environment/green-living-blog/2011/may/27/mark-zuckerberg-kill-animals-meat https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg-jack-dorsey-cold-goat-dinner-2019-1 ✎ Mark Zuckerberg took on one of the most surprising personal challenges I’ve ever seen. In this video, I walk you through the year he decided to eat only meat from animals he personally killed. Mark learned from farmers, chefs, and even his neighbor Jesse Cool to make sure he did it humanely. He shocked friends with posts like “I just killed a pig and a goat,” and even served Jack Dorsey a goat he cooked himself. This challenge pushed Mark to eat healthier, think deeper about gratitude, and understand the real cost of food. It also shows the same discipline he used to build Facebook from a Harvard dorm room into a global company. ✎ I also break down how Mark carried out the challenge step-by-step, from learning how to slaughter animals respectfully to becoming a part-time vegetarian for most of that year. You’ll hear how Michael Pollan reacted, why Jack Dorsey ended up eating only salad, and how the story spread around the world. Beyond the goat dinner, we go through the bigger pattern in Mark’s life: his yearly challenges. From learning Mandarin to writing daily thank-you notes, from meeting a new person every day to coding again daily, Mark used these projects to push himself and stay curious. These challenges helped him grow outside the boardroom and understand people, culture, and discipline on a deeper level. ✎ In the final section, I share why these challenges matter and what we can learn from them. Mark’s yearly missions remind us that success isn’t only about business. It’s about staying humble, stepping out of your comfort zone, and choosing growth even when you don’t have to. You don’t need to copy Mark’s goat challenge, but you can try something that stretches you just a little bit. When you do, you build discipline, confidence, and belief in yourself. If Mark Zuckerberg, Jack Dorsey, Jesse Cool, and even Michael Pollan can teach us anything here, it’s that small challenges can turn into big life lessons. episodes.title: Mark Zuckerberg & Priscilla Chan: How AI Will Help Cure Disease
episodes.description:
As part of our summer replay series, we're revisiting one of our favorite conversations from the past year.

Mark Zuckerberg and Dr. Priscilla Chan join Ben Horowitz, Vineeta Agarwala, and Erik Torenberg to discuss the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative's ambitious effort to help cure, prevent, and manage disease by the end of the century.

Rather than funding individual breakthroughs, CZI is focused on building the tools and infrastructure that can accelerate scientific discovery across entire fields. The conversation explores Biohub, Cell Atlas, virtual cell models, open biological datasets, and the growing role of AI in helping researchers better understand human biology.

They discuss why biology still lacks a "periodic table of elements," how AI could help scientists test hypotheses before running expensive experiments, and why pairing frontier biology with frontier AI may unlock a new era of medical discovery.

episodes.title: Mark Zuckerberg  [Facebook]: L'Homme Qui a Vendu Vos Données
episodes.description:
11 avril 2018. Mark Zuckerberg, 33 ans, témoigne devant le Congrès américain.

87 millions d'utilisateurs Facebook ont vu leurs données volées par Cambridge Analytica.

L'élection de 2016 a peut-être été manipulée. Le petit génie de Harvard qui voulait "connecter le monde" a créé une machine qui divise les démocraties.


Ceci est l'histoire vraie de Mark Zuckerberg. L'homme qui a transformé l'amitié en algorithme... et vos données en empire.


🎯 POINTS CLÉS DE L'HISTOIRE :

  • Comment Mark a volé l'idée de Facebook aux frères Winklevoss

  • La trahison d'Eduardo Saverin, cofondateur éjecté de l'entreprise

  • Le modèle économique : "Si c'est gratuit, vous êtes le produit"

  • Cambridge Analytica : 87 millions d'utilisateurs trahis

  • Les acquisitions stratégiques : Instagram (1 milliard $), WhatsApp (19 milliards $)

  • Le pivot vers Meta et la réalité virtuelle

  • 177 milliards $ de fortune personnelle... à quel prix ?

💡 CE QUE VOUS ALLEZ DÉCOUVRIR :

L'histoire complète de Mark Zuckerberg, du dortoir de Harvard au Congrès américain. Comment un étudiant de 19 ans a créé le réseau social le plus puissant de l'histoire... en trahissant tous ceux qui lui ont fait confiance. Les scandales, les manipulations, les acquisitions agressives, et la transformation de Facebook en Meta. Mark Zuckerberg a-t-il connecté le monde... ou l'a-t-il divisé ? Génie visionnaire ou manipulateur impitoyable ? À vous de juger.


📊 TRANSFORMATION AVANT/APRÈS :

AVANT (2004) : 19 ans, étudiant à Harvard, aucun revenu, socialement invisible APRÈS (2024) : 40 ans, 177 milliards $, 3 milliards d'utilisateurs, contrôle de Facebook, Instagram et WhatsApp 🔥


CITATIONS MARQUANTES :

"Si vous avez quelque chose que vous ne voulez pas que les gens sachent, peut-être ne devriez-vous pas le faire." - Mark Zuckerberg, 2009

"Les idées ne valent rien. C'est l'exécution qui compte." - Mark Zuckerberg


Hébergé par Ausha. Visitez ausha.co/politique-de-confidentialite pour plus d'informations.

episodes.title: Mark Zuckerberg - Finding your purpose isn't enough anymore motivational speech
episodes.description:
Mark Zuckerberg – Finding Your Purpose Isn’t Enough Anymore

In this thought-provoking episode, Mark Zuckerberg, tech visionary and Meta founder, challenges the conventional wisdom that simply finding your purpose is enough to succeed.
